s2-000-68c0176e32d77a98.wav.text: Start with pre tokenization, which people treat as plumbing and is not.

s2-001-2c639bf29d20ea9f.wav.text: BPE is greedy about frequency and has no notion of linguistic sense.

s2-002-219d7af65f62704e.wav.text: Left completely alone, it will cheerfully learn a token that spans the word the and a following newline, because that pair is genuinely frequent.

s2-003-b6c227439242439b.wav.text: Pre tokenization prevents that by splitting the text with a regular expression first, and running BPE strictly inside each chunk.

s2-004-580a09d0fe6bd46c.wav.text: No merge can ever cross a chunk boundary.

s2-005-38b8c875e8b54be0.wav.text: That is a hard constraint, not a preference.

s2-006-4b0622e8b7b632b7.wav.text: GPT two's regex is the reason its tokens carry a leading space.

s2-008-e78f562cc8bc97b0.wav.text: So the regex is a prior on which tokens can exist at all, chosen before a single byte of data is seen.

s2-009-45d27df5584349d7.wav.text: It is the one part of a tokenizer that is designed rather than learned, which makes it worth measuring rather than copying.

s3-000-0ca2bc949fa072bc.wav.text: Here is the finance variant, which is GPT two's pattern with three additions.

s3-001-09fa2c871cb507cc.wav.text: ISO dates become one chunk, where GPT two splits them into about five.

s3-002-fdf0a252d2daaa4e.wav.text: All caps runs, meaning tickers and ISINs, stay whole, so a symbol is one or two tokens rather than five.

s3-003-92d6711571c365e4.wav.text: And numbers group by thousands, where the important property is consistency rather than the specific grouping.

s3-004-1d4b0667c9437140.wav.text: Now look at the highlighted line near the bottom.

s3-005-3d425da53ea32cd4.wav.text: That branch, any remaining Unicode numeric, was not in the original design.

s3-006-ef032f29c98333ba.wav.text: It was added after the fuzzer found something, and that is the next scene.

s4-000-f0ceca5df75a117d.wav.text: Here is the bug, and it is my favourite kind, because it is invisible until you look for it in exactly the right way.

s4-001-b04d5f21ff9abcea.wav.text: The first version of this pattern used backslash d for its numeric branches.

s4-002-7356bef8168754d8.wav.text: And its fallback branch, the one that catches punctuation, excluded backslash p N, the Unicode numeric category.

s4-003-069dc47042878303.wav.text: Superscript two and superscript three are p N but they are not backslash d.

s4-004-4ffcec9570c5f543.wav.text: So no branch in the entire alternation matched them, findall skipped them, and the pre tokenizer silently deleted those characters from the text.

s4-005-197195c8d51da89f.wav.text: The tokenizer round tripped café and emoji flawlessly the whole time.

s4-007-e117c9c30a468bb2.wav.text: The fuzzer found it on the run where I fed it all two hundred and fifty six latin one bytes.

s4-008-104d83cf22c886c8.wav.text: A pre tokenizer must be total.

s4-009-a110eb8c749f9ea1.wav.text: Every character must be claimed by some branch.

s4-010-6401bf7663bb05a6.wav.text: There is now a regression test that runs every latin one byte and a twelve thousand code point sweep through both patterns.

s5-003-237ec5e3a6ff4c35.wav.text: End of text marks a document boundary and separates documents during pretraining.

s5-004-d61be7ccb50ba448.wav.text: Pad is masked out of the loss.

s5-005-b2ad00893f9a7abb.wav.text: And four semantic ones, saying which kind of financial text follows, which AlphaSLM will condition on.

s5-006-65d85eaa89581f56.wav.text: The requirement is that these must be unforgeable.

s5-007-43e80f15dd508f31.wav.text: Their entire job is to mean something that no amount of ordinary text can counterfeit.

s5-008-4e375f337e7e2f86.wav.text: So they are matched before BPE runs, and their ids are reserved above the learned vocabulary where no merge can ever produce them.

s5-009-6df79700ea84461b.wav.text: The bottom two lines are the proof, and it is a test in the suite.

s6-000-4bd4aa7a8ff6e829.wav.text: And here is the measurement, set up as carefully as I could make it.

s6-001-9d113008836897e3.wav.text: Same trainer, same requested vocabulary size, same pre tokenizer, both truncated to exactly nine hundred and ninety seven merges so the vocabularies are identical in size.

s6-002-db9ff1d37adc5590.wav.text: The only thing that differs is the corpus each was trained on.

s6-003-572bfd62b0e0cc32.wav.text: Both are then measured on held out financial text that neither saw.

s6-004-28530b30d5351b3a.wav.text: FinTok gets four point five two eight bytes per token.

s6-005-678807057fb92c53.wav.text: The general English vocabulary gets one point six five eight.

s6-006-face39fa293c81ed.wav.text: Raw bytes, the floor, is one.

s6-007-dbf4b26f30345d22.wav.text: So the domain vocabulary is two point seven three times more compact on the domain it was built for.

s6-008-13a6b478f603f851.wav.text: And notice the middle bar is still well above the floor.

s6-009-4e435d3d8285ef92.wav.text: Even a completely mismatched vocabulary learns English morphology that transfers.

s7-000-87dac6ea1dce2f9d.wav.text: It is worth being precise about what that two point seven three actually buys, because compression sounds like a vanity metric and is not.

s7-001-b0de072243dc17c8.wav.text: Bytes per token is the exchange rate between your text and everything the model costs.

s7-002-9d4e47b28bfbd6f7.wav.text: Two point seven three times more text fits in the same context window.

s7-003-b7d94f3902d68f4e.wav.text: Two point seven three times fewer positions to attend over, and since attention cost grows with the square of length, the saving there is considerably larger than the ratio.

s7-004-efdc66ba35a4ec95.wav.text: Two point seven three times fewer forward passes to generate the same amount of output text, because generation is one forward pass per token.

s7-006-f86c6fdd0b72d70a.wav.text: Domain phrases become single tokens instead of fragments, so the model has less structure to learn from scratch.

s7-007-93f8958353c56a1e.wav.text: Two hundred lines of code, run once, before any training starts.
